methodologyMain.h1: How we read the chronobiology literature.
methodologyMain.intro: CircadianStack publishes Protocol cards. Every dose carries a citation to the trial it came from. The page you are reading is the short version. The long-form, versioned spec lives at
methodologyMain.scoreTitle: A 0-100 confidence score for the protocols on this site.
methodologyMain.scoreBody: Stack Score is not a product rating. It is a confidence score for a protocol — morning light at 10,000 lux for 30 minutes, for instance. Five weighted dimensions feed the number, and the tier label tells you how much weight to put on it.
methodologyMain.reviewersBody: Protocols touching sleep disorders (DSPD, shift work disorder, suspected non-24) carry a reviewer stamp at the top of the page. Reviewers are board-certified sleep physicians or chronobiology PhDs. Names and credentials show up on every reviewed protocol.
methodologyMain.r1b: Every dose, window, and wavelength claim links to the published trial — Khalsa, Zeitzer, Lockley, Roenneberg, by name — never to a podcast clip or content marketer.
methodologyMain.r2b: Light therapy lamps measured with a lux meter at 12, 18, and 24 inches. Sunrise alarms measured at pillow distance. Melatonin cited at physiological doses (0.3-0.5 mg) as the default.
methodologyMain.r3b: Every protocol ships with a Failure modes section: who it is wrong for, where the dose-response relationship breaks, what the trial population missed.
methodologyMain.r4b: We do not accept payment from lamp manufacturers, supplement brands, or sleep-tracker companies for editorial coverage. Affiliate commissions exist on some links and never change rankings.
methodologyMain.r5t: We update when new chronobiology drops.
methodologyMain.r5b: Trial readouts and major-label updates trigger a protocol refresh. Updated dates show on every Protocol card.

methodologyPage.metaDescription: How CircadianStack reports on circadian biology and sleep. A public methodology, versioned like software, updated when better evidence makes the previous version look incomplete.
methodologyPage.intro: Every protocol on this site is checked against the same five-step rubric. The rubric is public, versioned, and updated when better chronobiology data makes the previous version look thin.

methodologyV12.intro: Five weighted dimensions feed a single 0-100 score. The score gets rounded, mapped to a tier, and shown next to protocols that need a confidence tag. This page is the long-form spec.
methodologyV12.reviewersTitle: Who signs off, in plain language.
methodologyV12.reviewersBody: Protocols that touch a sleep disorder (DSPD, shift work disorder, non-24) get reviewed by a board-certified sleep physician or a chronobiology PhD before publish. The reviewer name and credentials live on the protocol and on the author bio.
methodologyV12.dim1High: Multi-arm randomized trial with pre-registered endpoints, or a meta-analysis covering several independent labs.
methodologyV12.dim1Mid: Single trial with limitations like open-label design or single-site recruiting.
methodologyV12.dim1Low: Animal data, case series, or anecdotal report only.
methodologyV12.dim2High: Receptor or photoreceptor pathway established and reproduced (melanopsin / melatonin / SCN signalling).
methodologyV12.dim2Mid: Plausible mechanism with one or two supporting studies.
methodologyV12.dim2Low: Hypothetical pathway, or mechanism borrowed from a different system.
methodologyV12.dim3High: Two or more independent labs report consistent dose-response curves.
methodologyV12.dim3Mid: One large trial plus supportive observational work.
methodologyV12.dim4High: The protocol fits the day a real reader actually has — wake time, work schedule, home lighting.
methodologyV12.dim4Mid: Protocol works with one schedule constraint reshuffled.
methodologyV12.dim4Low: Lab-only, or requires bespoke equipment unavailable to most readers.
methodologyV12.dim5High: No reported adverse events in trial populations matching our reader; risk profile well-characterized.
methodologyV12.dim5Mid: Mild adverse events at dose; manageable with timing or stepwise titration.
methodologyV12.dim5Low: Adverse events common, contraindicated populations significant, or risk under-characterized.
methodologyV12.tier1: We treat this as settled enough to act on. Independent replication exists, mechanism is clear, the protocol fits a typical reader's day.
methodologyV12.tier2: Solid evidence, but one of the five dimensions is short of perfect — usually replication or practicality.
methodologyV12.tier3: Worth running, with caveats stated in the body of the protocol.
methodologyV12.tier4: Early signal. We publish because readers ask, and we flag exactly what is missing.
methodologyV12.tier5: Mechanism is plausible or the anecdote is loud, but the trial literature is too thin to be confident. We say so in plain language.
methodologyV12.cl12: Added Practicality as a fifth dimension; rebalanced weights so Trial strength still dominates at 35%. Tier band names now read HIGH CONFIDENCE / STRONG / MODERATE / LIMITED / PRELIMINARY.
methodologyV12.cl11: Added Reproducibility as a separate dimension instead of being folded into Trial strength.
methodologyV12.cl10: Initial spec. Three dimensions: Trial strength, Mechanism, Safety.
